title: How Ross Jenkins built a $2M freelance email agency: personality, niching, and pricing by demand
summary: Ross Jenkins, an Upwork top earner turned agency founder, explains why personal, story-led email still sells and why past clients are an overlooked gold mine. He also covers niching into a specialism, raising rates as demand grows, and turning away clients who haggle on price.

principles.text: Make emails read like they come from a real person; personality is what sells and email is not dead.
principles.quote: no one wants to reply to a robot um or a no reply email address or you know personality sells and that's what that's what people forget

principles.text: Email your past client list. It is the simplest, most overlooked revenue lever, and people are just scared to hit send.
principles.quote: if you email your past Client List and you've got a sale on or you've got you know you want to update them about news it's honestly a gold mine most companies miss it out

principles.text: Give people a concrete reason to opt in to your list instead of a generic 'join my newsletter' ask.
principles.quote: you want to give them a reason to opt in and normally people would be like that's a no-brainer I'm going to click it

principles.text: Niche down to one specialism; generalists get generalist pay, and buyers hire specialists for each part of a job.
principles.quote: it's about niching down and that's why why I you know I specialize in email marketing you know that's our main bread and butter

principles.text: Raise your price as demand for your time grows, and don't accept rates below your average, since low-ball buyers signal how they'll behave.
principles.quote: when we see huge sort of uproars in demand in terms of my time we know it's time to increase the the hourly rate

principles.text: Hold yourself and hires to delivering at least double the value you are paid, and know your ROI so you can price with confidence.
principles.quote: I want you to be able to add at least double the value that I'm paying you so if I'm paying you $100 an hour I want you to be able to make me $200 an hour
